overview: Harden Rainbow AI's external system integrations (PMS2/DIGIMAN, fnb-online-ordering, future systems). Make integration easy for non-technical users, add fault tolerance with retry/circuit-breaker at HTTP layer, improve troubleshooting with clear diagnostics, and make connections robust with health monitoring. Currently: http-client.ts has zero retry, zero circuit-breaker, hardcoded 30s timeout, and cryptic error messages.
goals: HTTP client retries transient failures automatically with exponential backoff
Circuit breaker prevents hammering a dead external API
Integration errors produce clear, actionable troubleshooting messages
Admin dashboard shows real-time health of all external connections
New integrations can be added with minimal configuration via IntegrationClient
Setup validator catches misconfigurations before they hit production

userStories.title: Add HTTP retry with exponential backoff to http-client.ts
userStories.description: The current http-client.ts makes a single attempt to call the DIGIMAN API. If the network hiccups or the server returns 502/503, the request fails immediately. WhatsApp sending already has retry logic (send-retry.ts), but the HTTP client does not. Add automatic retry with exponential backoff for transient failures (network errors, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504). Non-retryable errors (400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422) should fail immediately. This is the single highest-impact change for robustness.
acceptanceCriteria: callAPI retries up to 3 times on transient failures (network error, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504)
Backoff is exponential: ~1s, ~2s, ~4s (with ±20% jitter to prevent thundering herd)
Non-retryable status codes (400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422) fail immediately without retry
Each retry logs a warning with attempt number, error, and endpoint
Total timeout across all retries does not exceed 45 seconds
Retry behavior can be disabled per-call via options parameter
npm run build succeeds
Existing tests still pass
technicalNotes: File to modify: src/lib/http-client.ts
Pattern: Use axios-retry or implement manually (prefer manual to avoid new dependency)
Add retry options to callAPI signature: callAPI<T>(method, path, data?, options?: { retry?: boolean, maxRetries?: number, timeoutMs?: number })
Retryable status codes: 429, 500, 502, 503, 504, ECONNRESET, ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEDOUT, EPIPE
For 429 (rate limit): respect Retry-After header if present
Keep the existing error message format but enhance with retry context: 'API Error (after 3 retries): ...'
Log format: [HTTP] Retry {attempt}/{max} for {method} {path}: {error} (next in {delay}ms)

userStories.title: Add circuit breaker for DIGIMAN API calls
userStories.description: Rainbow AI already has a CircuitBreaker for AI providers (src/assistant/circuit-breaker.ts) but the DIGIMAN HTTP client has no circuit breaker. When the PMS is down, every guest interaction triggers a 30-second timeout — multiplied across concurrent guests, this saturates the connection pool and blocks the event loop. Add a circuit breaker to http-client.ts that wraps callAPI. Use the existing CircuitBreaker class from circuit-breaker.ts — do NOT create a new one.
acceptanceCriteria: A CircuitBreaker instance wraps DIGIMAN API calls in http-client.ts
After 5 consecutive failures, circuit opens and fast-fails for 60 seconds
Fast-fail throws a clear error: 'DIGIMAN API circuit is OPEN — API appears down, skipping call to {path}. Will retry after cooldown.'
After 60s cooldown, one test request is allowed (HALF_OPEN state)
Success in HALF_OPEN closes the circuit (normal operation resumes)
Circuit breaker status is exposed via getDigimanCircuitStatus() export
npm run build succeeds
Existing tests still pass
technicalNotes: File to modify: src/lib/http-client.ts
Import CircuitBreaker from '../assistant/circuit-breaker.js' — reuse existing class
Create a module-level instance: const digimanCircuit = new CircuitBreaker('digiman-api', { failureThreshold: 5, cooldownMs: 60000 })
In callAPI: check digimanCircuit.isOpen() BEFORE making the request. If open, throw immediately.
On success: call digimanCircuit.recordSuccess()
On retryable failure (after all retries exhausted): call digimanCircuit.recordFailure()
On non-retryable failure (4xx): do NOT record as circuit breaker failure (those are client errors, not server issues)
Export function getDigimanCircuitStatus() that returns digimanCircuit.getStatus()
This integrates with US-201 retry — circuit breaker wraps the retry loop

This gives operators a single place to check if everything is working. Currently the only health info is the /health/ready endpoint which returns a simple ok/degraded string — we need structured data showing each integration's status, last success time, error count, and circuit breaker state.

Response includes: WhatsApp connection status (connected/disconnected)
Response includes: Database connection status (connected/error)
Each integration shows: name, status, lastSuccessAt, lastErrorAt, errorCount5m, circuitState, avgResponseMs

Register in src/routes/admin/index.ts alongside other admin routes
For DIGIMAN: import getDigimanCircuitStatus from http-client.ts (from US-202), add request timing tracking

userStories.title: Add integration setup validator and troubleshooting diagnostics
userStories.description: Create a setup validator that runs at startup AND can be triggered via admin API. It checks all integration prerequisites (env vars set, URLs reachable, tokens valid, ports open) and provides clear, actionable fix instructions when something is wrong. Currently, misconfiguration produces cryptic axios errors. This is the 'easy for dummies' feature — instead of 'ECONNREFUSED', say 'Cannot reach PMS at http://localhost:5000. Is the PMS server running? Try: 1) Check DIGIMAN_API_URL in .env, 2) Verify the PMS is started, 3) Check firewall rules.'
acceptanceCriteria: New module src/lib/integration-validator.ts exports validateIntegrations() function
Validates: DIGIMAN_API_URL is set and reachable, DIGIMAN_API_TOKEN is set and not expired, DATABASE_URL is set and connectable
Each check returns: { name, status: 'ok'|'warning'|'error', message, fix? }
Fix messages are plain English with numbered steps, not technical jargon
validateIntegrations() runs at server startup (non-blocking, logs results)
GET /api/admin/diagnostics endpoint triggers full validation and returns results
Diagnostics include system info: node version, memory usage, uptime, env vars (redacted)
npm run build succeeds
technicalNotes: Create: src/lib/integration-validator.ts
Create: src/routes/admin/diagnostics.ts (register in admin/index.ts)
Validation checks in order: 1) env vars present, 2) URL format valid, 3) DNS resolves, 4) TCP connect, 5) HTTP health endpoint responds, 6) Auth token accepted
For DIGIMAN: try GET /api/health, if fails try GET /api/occupancy (some deployments don't have /health)
For Database: try a simple query via the existing db connection
Error-to-fix mapping examples:
ECONNREFUSED → 'PMS server is not running at {url}. Start it with: cd pms2 && npm run dev'
401 Unauthorized → 'API token is invalid or expired. Update DIGIMAN_API_TOKEN in .env'
ENOTFOUND → 'Cannot resolve hostname {host}. Check DIGIMAN_API_URL spelling and DNS'
ETIMEDOUT → 'Connection to {url} timed out. Check firewall rules and network connectivity'
Redact sensitive env vars: show first 4 + last 4 chars of tokens, full URLs
Call validateIntegrations() in src/index.ts after server starts (fire-and-forget)

userStories.title: Add configurable per-endpoint timeout and request tracking
userStories.description: The current http-client.ts has a hardcoded 30-second timeout for ALL API calls. Some endpoints are fast (GET /api/health = 200ms) and some are slow (POST /api/units/assign with complex booking = 10s). Add per-call timeout configuration and lightweight request tracking (for the health dashboard in US-203). Also reduce the default timeout from 30s to 15s — 30s is too long to block a WhatsApp conversation.
acceptanceCriteria: Default timeout reduced from 30000ms to 15000ms
callAPI options parameter supports timeoutMs override: callAPI('GET', '/path', null, { timeoutMs: 5000 })
Request tracker records: last success timestamp, last error timestamp, rolling error count (5-min window), average response time (last 20 requests)
Request tracker exported via getRequestStats() function
Error messages include timing info: 'API Error (took 15.2s, timed out): ...'
npm run build succeeds
Existing tests still pass

Add RequestTracker class (or simple object) at module level to track stats
Track: lastSuccessAt, lastErrorAt, recentErrors (array of {timestamp, path, error}), responseTimes (last 20)
In callAPI: record start time, on success record response time, on error record to tracker
Clean up recentErrors older than 5 minutes on each call (simple sliding window)
getRequestStats() returns: { lastSuccessAt, lastErrorAt, errorCount5m, avgResponseMs, totalRequests }

userStories.title: Enhance error messages with actionable troubleshooting hints
userStories.description: Currently http-client.ts error messages say things like 'API Error: /api/units 503. Check DIGIMAN_API_URL'. This is not helpful for non-technical users. Enhance ALL error paths to include: what happened, why it might have happened, and what to do about it. Use a troubleshooting hint map that maps error codes/types to plain-English explanations. Also add a troubleshooting section to the admin dashboard.
acceptanceCriteria: Error messages follow format: 'What: {description}. Why: {likely cause}. Fix: {action steps}'
Network errors (ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEDOUT, ENOTFOUND) produce specific troubleshooting hints
HTTP errors (401, 403, 404, 500, 502, 503) produce specific hints
Circuit breaker OPEN state produces a clear explanation and ETA for next retry
Admin WhatsApp notification on persistent failures (>3 consecutive) includes troubleshooting steps
npm run build succeeds
technicalNotes: File to modify: src/lib/http-client.ts
Create a troubleshootingHints map: Record<string, { why: string, fix: string }>
Map keys: ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEDOUT, ENOTFOUND, ECONNRESET, 401, 403, 404, 500, 502, 503, 504, CIRCUIT_OPEN
Example: ECONNREFUSED → { why: 'The PMS server is not accepting connections', fix: '1) Check if PMS is running 2) Verify DIGIMAN_API_URL in .env 3) Check firewall rules' }
Example: 503 → { why: 'PMS server is overloaded or restarting', fix: 'Wait 30 seconds and retry. If persistent, check PMS server logs and memory usage.' }

Example: CIRCUIT_OPEN → { why: 'Too many consecutive failures — circuit breaker activated to protect system', fix: 'Circuit will auto-recover in {cooldown}s. Check PMS health: curl {url}/api/health' }
Notification: import notifyAdminConfigError from admin-notifier.ts, send after 3+ consecutive failures
